meta.title: Report Review Quick Start
meta.purpose: Give each role one page with the steps to review a report and record results
sources: Synthetic example content for the document-builder skill; replace with the request and cited sources

blocks.text: Anyone asked to check a report before it is released. You need access to the test queue, the report under review and the expected results for each test.

items: Record a result for each step.
Attach a screenshot when a step fails.
Open the test from your queue and read the expected result.
Follow each step on the report exactly as written, one step at a time.
Record **Pass** or **Fail** for the step and add a note on a failure.
Select **Submit** when every step has a result.

blocks.title: A Failed Step
blocks.text: The total on the summary page does not match the total on the detail page. Record **Fail** for the step, note both numbers in the comment, attach a screenshot of each page and move on to the next step.

items: Submitting before every step has a result.
Recording a failure without a note.

blocks.text: Ask your review lead when a step is unclear, the expected result looks wrong or the report does not open. Include the test name and the step number.
The person who assigns tests to testers, answers their questions during the review and decides when a report is ready to release.

items: Send failures back for a fix and a retest.
Assign each test to one tester and set a due date in the queue.
Open each submitted test and read every result and note.
Log each failure with the tester's note and screenshot.
Approve the report when every failure is fixed and retested.

blocks.title: A Retest
blocks.text: A tester records a failure on the summary total. Log the failure with the tester's note, wait for the fix, then assign the same test again and review the new result before you approve the report.

items: Approving the report while a failure is still open.
Assigning one test to two testers at the same time.

blocks.text: Contact the report owner when a failure needs a decision on scope, or when two testers record different results for the same step.
